Senses.Explanation: (丹霄獨步, to walk alone through the red heavens) is Xuedou Chongxian's closing invitation on the Zhimen case, born in his own record: the clam holds the bright moon, the rabbit conceives; this not only locks the world fast, it settles the realm in peace — if you can weigh it well, pray walk alone through the red heavens. The Yuan masters fix the partner line before it — the great function present before you, walk alone through the red heavens — at Gulin Qingmao's temple entry and Liao'an Qingyu's hall address; and when Qingmao re-weighs the old man's verdict he gives its author twenty blows for having no way out. Yuanwu Keqin carries it three times — the Jinshan entry address above the second-meaning gate, the direct-taking address that goes hand in hand with the sages, and the Blue Cliff Record's case-7 recommendation; the Song halls hand the invitation down — Changling's cliff-face, Huitang's road-head, Ying'an's seat-taking net, Xiatang's two-mistakes fork. The root. Xuedou Chongxian raises the Zhimen case — what is the body of complete discernment? a clam holding the bright moon; what is its function? a rabbit conceiving — and rules: not only does it lock the world fast, it settles the realm in peace; if you can weigh it well, pray walk alone through the red heavens. The Yuan masters pair the line with the great function: Gulin Qingmao, entering the Kaiyuan temple at Pingjiang, points at the mountain gate — entering you see the plaque, mounting you see the road; the great function present before you, walk alone through the red heavens; his disciple Liao'an Qingyu, in his own hall address, sets the enigma-line before it (the character 以 does not complete it, the character 八 is not it). When Gulin Qingmao re-raises the case he quotes Xuedou's verdict whole — writing (安貼󳬛家, with the composite graph) where the root writes (安貼邦家) — and then turns on the old man himself: this one has, after all, no way out — a good twenty blows; his same-birth-same-death, releasing and gathering, is son succeeding father. Yuanwu Keqin carries it three ways. Entering Jinshan under imperial summons he tells the assembly that before crossing Guazhou he had already given them the one sentence — take it by mind or thought, eye or ear, and you miss it; even the far side of Yinzhi before the seven buddhas is still talk; take it in whole, no need for what-now — pray walk alone through the red heavens, or fall into the gate of the second meaning. In the direct-taking address the invitation rides on the picture of the man who can receive it — teeth like a sword-forest, mouth like a blood-basin, one blow and no turning back; heaven heaven, earth earth, not one hair-tip stirred: taking it on direct, you can walk alone through the red heavens and go hand in hand with the sages. And in the Blue Cliff Record's case 7, after opening Fayan Wenyi's answer to Huichao — you are Huichao — he sets the same bar: recommended right there, you may walk alone through the red heavens; construe it emotionally and it is three lifetimes sixty kalpas. The Song halls hand the invitation down. Changling Shouzhuo, old and hard of hearing, still holds out the old tag — no night-travel allowed, you must arrive by dawn — then the vinegar-worm that does not know sour, the mirror that does not shine on itself; but you who once let go your hand on the ten-thousand-fathom cliff face — pray walk alone through the red heavens. Huitang Zuxin points: the blue-cloud road lies right before your eyes; where is the road-head? He lifts the whisk — right here; a keen-witted fellow sees it once. Ying'an Tanhua, taking the abbot's seat at Baoen Guangxiao in Pingjiang, calls the room the net that canopies the sky — those who get through it get a hammer behind the skull as well; those who cannot — best walk alone through the red heavens; to kill a man you must see blood, to help a man you must help him through. Xiatang Huiyuan builds his two mistakes — wrong on the sutra line, wrong on Yunfeng Wenyue's marketplace line — and sets the fork: grasp the mountain monk's two wrongs and you climb the high peak hand in hand; if not, walk alone through the red heavens as you will; and after a pause he restates the same fork in his own name: grasp the two wrongs and buddhas and patriarchs are shelved from the start. Verses, challenges, and the sea crossing. Xutang Zhiyu's coffin verse for the senior monk Zhu of Yongjia — dwelling, it is not a temple; a temple, it does not dwell — walks the iron-wall silver-mountain line into the red heavens, the wild ape crying at the third watch. Duanqiao Miaolun opens his summer examination: ninety days without one gesture or one phrase makes a laureate of the Chan examination — so is there anyone in the assembly who walks alone through the red heavens, comes out and overturns the Chan seat and shouts the assembly apart? If you are not a guest of Dragon Gate, beware the mark on the forehead. Chushi Fanqi assigns office with it — in the Vulture-Peak mountain by capacity, on the Cao-Stream road little substance much vanity; no matter the shallow-field commoner, pray walk alone through the red heavens. And in Japan, Koho Kennichi, heir of Wuxue Zuyuan, allows it to his assembly after the stringless-zither exchange — the sentence before sound, ears crossed and mistaken; if you gentlemen get it, I allow you to walk alone through the red heavens. The Ming and Qing masters take it into their own settings. Mingjue Cong, summoned by the Buddha-Heart Son of Heaven, counts the silent ones — the World-Honored's flower, Linji Yixuan's shout, Deshan's blow — hands that cut nails without a mechanism reaching through; arrived here himself with nowhere to hide his body, he can only walk alone through the red heavens, and at once asks what that means under the gracious summons into the ninefold palace. Muchen Daomin answers for the assembly that cannot say who felled the cassia in the moon — it goes to the man who walks alone through the red heavens. Foyuan Chegang, raising Linji and Attendant Wang's exchange — neither reading sutras nor sitting in Chan, yet made buddha and patriarch; gold dust films the eye — rules: give me back progenitor Ji's pecking-egg opportunity; the Attendant must needs walk alone through the red heavens — who dare cross blows with the whetted blade?. Jifei Ruyi casts it into rhyme on a bell — the bell is cast of bronze, a blabbermouth pointing and glossing; a soul-mate beyond the frame, walk alone through the red heavens. Xiaotang Yunfen seals a coffin with it — the bhagavats of the ten directions, the one gate of nirvana; let it be the spring hue filling the garden — pray walk alone through the red heavens. Anthologies and sermons close the trail. Muyun Tongmen's nien on Zhaozhou Congshen's choosing case — someone once asked Zhou and for five years he could not settle the accounts; Xuedou Chongxian: words that cannot be turned, dead and done, twenty blows, and the blow must have somewhere to be handed down — repeats both verdicts, calls them causeless, says one word — blind — and closes: whoever can tell that out is assured of walking alone through the red heavens; his nien rides in the Raising-Old-Cases Anthology, nowhere in his own records. Tianyin Yuanxiu, preaching after Yantou Quanhuo's line that proclamation must flow from desirelessness, raises the whisk against Shakyamuni's flower — same or different? — still a handle fitted to the bowl; yet if you can pick it up, walk alone through the red heavens, free and unbound, knowing the mind-to-mind seal. And the lamp anchor: Xiaoyan Debao, on Yunmen's water-moon case that Yuanwu Keqin had already ruled lost by one chip, lifts his staff — if you gentlemen get these three turning words, you do not merely walk alone through the red heavens, you can be teacher to the men of the world — a nien carried only in the Tier-3 Grove of the Mirror of the School, kept after the gate was met and never toward it.

Senses.Explanation: The expression denotes Danxia burns the wooden buddha in these Chan records. Its wording is ‘Danxia burns a buddha’; in the narrated case the referent is explicitly a wooden buddha-image. The phrase has 14 exact occurrences in 8 source files representing 8 works. The repeated account says that, finding it cold at Huilin monastery, Danxia Tianran took a wooden buddha and burned it for a fire. When the temple officer rebuked him for burning ‘my wooden buddha,’ Danxia stirred the ashes with his staff and said he was looking for relics. The officer answered that a wooden buddha has no relics; Danxia then requested two more images to burn. The record adds that afterward the officer's eyebrows and beard fell out. Later masters preserve this as a numbered public case, ask whether Danxia's own eyebrows remain, warn against denying cause and effect, and group it in one roster with Manjusri holding the sword, Guizong cutting the snake, and Muzhou shutting the door. One later verse explicitly calls the deed ‘not light,’ mentions the officer's facial hair, and says that what one does one receives. These are the corpus's narrated actions and comments; this entry does not acquit or condemn Danxia.

Senses.Note: Xuedou recasts Xiangyan’s image of a person hanging from a branch by the mouth while someone below asks a question: speaking in the tree is easy; speaking below it is hard. Senses.PreferredTarget: I earnestly tell those who seek the mystery: do not let your time pass in vain
AlternateTargets: A word to those investigating the subtle: do not waste the passing hours
SearchAliases: seekers of mystery do not waste time
Senses.Note: Shitou closes his Cantongqi with an earnest warning to those seeking the mystery not to waste time. Miyun, Zhe'an, Shiyu, and Jiqi cite the old words and each turns them into a fresh question for an assembly. Hanyue, Yikui, and Azi voice the pair in present sermons with staff or whisk gestures and further challenges. The urgency lies in the current encounter: repeating the warning is itself no answer to how time is used.
